title: Alcohol use disorder: severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's alcohol use, if any is reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for alcohol use disorder and general health maintenance.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up. He reports feeling well overall and expresses a desire to maintain his current healthy lifestyle. Regarding his history of substance use, he reports that he has not consumed any alcohol for over a year. He remains committed to his sobriety and reports no cravings or difficulties maintaining his current status. He denies any recent falls, significant changes in sleep patterns, or new physical complaints. He continues to engage in regular light walking and remains active in his local community.

Medication List
1. Lisinopril 10mg daily
2. Atorvastatin 20mg daily
3. Multivitamin daily

Vitals
BP: 132/78 mmHg
HR: 72 bpm
RR: 16 breaths/min
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Height: 5'10"
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.8%
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
LDL: 88 mg/dL

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies any fevers, chills, or night sweats. He reports no changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency. He denies any new-onset joint pain or muscle weakness. He reports stable mood and no concerns regarding his memory or cognitive function.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives with his wife in a single-story home. He enjoys gardening and playing chess. He does not smoke and has not used other substances.

Family History
Father: Deceased, history of hypertension.
Mother: Deceased, history of type 2 diabetes.

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally; no wheezes or crackles.
Abdominal: Soft, non-tender, non-distended.
Neurological: Normal gait; intact strength and sensation in all extremities.

Assessment
1. Alcohol use disorder, mild: The patient is currently in sustained remission. He has successfully avoided alcohol consumption for over one year and shows high motivation for continued sobriety.
2. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current medication.
3. Hyperlipidemia: Stable on current statin therapy.

Plan
1. Alcohol use disorder, mild: Continue to provide supportive counseling and reinforce positive coping mechanisms. Encourage continued avoidance of alcohol.
2. Hypertension: Continue Lisinopril 10mg daily. Monitor blood pressure at next visit.
3. Hyperlipidemia: Continue Atorvastatin 20mg daily.
4. Follow-up: Return to clinic in 3 months for routine monitoring.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
October 14, 2026
explanations: Alcohol use disorder, mild, in remission: F10.11.

distractors.why: A mild use disorder is abuse (F10.1-), not dependence.
